1509025.initial:
Qatest RADIUS user (as the member of group1) is logged in to the firewall and can access the Internet.
Qalab RADIUS user (as the member of group2) is not allowed to log in. "User login denied" log message is shown on the Log>View page of the firewall.
1509025.title: Use RADIUS, RADIUS Filter-ID attribute on RADIUS server
1509025.result:
1) Load the firmware on the firewall and boot with default settings.
  2) Configure X0 (LAN), X1 (WAN), and X2 (DMZ) interfaces.
  3) Have RADIUS server connected on the LAN interface (IAS is used in this test case). Have a PC connected to the DMZ. Make sure that a user on the DMZ can access the Internet.
  4) On the Users>Settings page, select RADIUS as Authentication Method. Click the Configure button.
  5) Enter valid data in the Name or IP Address, Port Number, and Shared Secret fields on the Settings tab of the RADIUS Configuration window.
  6) Select Use RADIUS Filter-ID attribute on RADIUS server on the RADIUS Users tab. Apply and click OK.
  7) Configure RADIUS server. Create user groups group1 and group2 in Active Directory. Create a user qatest and make it a member of group1. Create a user qalab and make it a member of group2. Make sure that Allow Access on the Dial-in tab is selected in the users' Properties.
  8) Add a new access policy in IAS. Name it group1. Edit properties for group1 policy. Click Add to specify the condition to match. Select Windows-Groups and add group1. Click Edit Profile in group1 Properties. Click the Advanced tab, and then ckick Add. Select Filter-ID parameter in the list and double-click it. Click Add in Multivalued Attribute Information dialog. Select String in Enter the attribute value in and type group1. Click OK, and then click OK again to return to Multivaluated Attribute Information dialog. Save the changes in the profile and click OK in group1 Properties.
  9) Add a new access policy in IAS. Name it group2. Configure this policy the same way as described for group1 but set type to group2.
  10) On the Users>Local Groups page, add group1.
  11) On the Firewall>Access Rules page, modify the DMZ>WAN access rule. Select group1 in the Users Allowed field. Add DNS allow rule for All users.
  12) Access the Internet from the DMZ. When the LoginRedirect window is displayed, click on the link to access the auth.html window. Login as qatest. Attempt to login as qalab.

1509030.title: Use RADIUS + Local Users
1509030.result:
1) Load the firmware on the firewall and boot with default settings.
2) Configure X0 (LAN), X1 (WAN), and X2 (DMZ) interfaces.
3) Have RADIUS server connected on the LAN interface (IAS is used in this test case). Have a PC connected to the DMZ. Make sure that a user on the DMZ can access the Internet.
4) On the Users>Settings page, select RADIUS as Authentication Method. Click the Configure button.
5) Enter valid data in the Name or IP Address, Port Number, and Shared Secret fields on the Settings tab of the RADIUS Configuration window.
6) Select Use RADIUS Filter-ID attribute on RADIUS server on the RADIUS Users tab and also use the same filter ID in "Default user group to which all RADIUS users belong" for authentication to work. Apply and click OK.
7) On the Firewall>Access Rules page, modify the DMZ>WAN access rule. Select Everyone in the Users Allowed field. Add DNS allow rule for All users.
8) Configure RADIUS server. Create a user group group1 in Active Directory. Create a user qatest and make it a member of group1. Make sure that Allow Access on the Dial-in tab is selected in the user's Properties.
9) Add a new access policy in IAS. Name it group1. Edit properties for group1 policy. Click Add to specify the condition to match. Select Windows-Groups and add group1. Click Edit Profile in group1 Properties. Click the Advanced tab, and then ckick Add. Select Filter-ID parameter in the list and double-click it. Click Add in Multivalued Attribute Information dialog. Select String in Enter the attribute value in and type group1. Click OK, and then click OK again to return to Multivaluated Attribute Information dialog. Save the changes in the profile and click OK in group1 Properties.
10) On the Users>Local Users page of the SonicWALL, add a new user user1.
11) Access the Internet from the DMZ. When the LoginRedirect window is displayed, click on the link to access the auth.html window. Login as qatest and user1.

1509027.title: SonicWALL vendor-specific attribute on RADIUS server. Memberships can be set locally by duplicating RADIUS user names. Allow only users listed locally.
1509027.result:
1) Load the firmware on the firewall and boot with default settings.
2) Configure X0 (LAN) and X1 (WAN) interfaces.
3) Have a PC with the RADIUS server connected on the LAN interface (IAS is used in this test case). Make sure that a user on the LAN can access the Internet.
4) On the Users>Settings page, select RADIUS as Authentication Method. Click the Configure button.
5) Enter valid data in the Name or IP Address, Port Number, and Shared Secret fields on the Settings tab of the RADIUS Configuration window.
6) Select Use SonicWALL vendor-specific attribute on RADIUS server on the RADIUS Users tab. Check the Memberships can be set locally by duplicating RADIUS user names check box. Check the Allow only users listed locally check box. Apply and click OK.
7) On the Users>Local groups page, add a new group. Name it grouptest. Add Limited Administrators default group to the grouptest.
8) On the Users>Local Users page, add a user test1. Add test1 to the group grouptest.
9) On the Users>Local Users page, add a user qatest1.
10) On the Firewall>Access Rules page, modify the LAN>WAN access rule. Select grouptest in the Users Allowed field. Add DNS allow rule for All users.
11) Configure RADIUS server. Create user groups group1 and group2 in Active Directory. Create users qatest1 and qatest2 and make them members of group1. Create users test1 and test2 and make them members of group2. Make sure that Allow Access on the Dial-in tab is selected in the users' Properties.
12) Add a new access policy in IAS. Name it group1. Edit properties for group1 policy. Click Add to specify the condition to match. Select Windows-Groups and add group1. Click Edit Profile in group1 Properties. Click the Advanced tab, and then ckick Add. Select Vendor-Specific parameter in the list and double-click it. Click Add in Multivalued Attribute Information dialog. In the Vendor-Specific Attribute Information window, select the Enter Vendor Code. Type vendor code 8741 (for SonicWALL). Select Yes. It conforms. Click the Configure Attribute button. In the Configure VSA window, enter Vendor-assigned attribute nubmer - 1, Attribute Format - Decimal, Attribute value - 5 (Limited Management). Click OK, and then click OK again to return to Multivaluated Attribute Information dialog. Save the changes in the profile and click OK in group1 Properties.
13) Add a new access policy in IAS. Name it group2. Configure this policy the same way as described for group1 but set Attribute value to 2 (Bypass Filters).
14) Log out from the SonicWALL. Access the Internet from the LAN. When the LoginRedirect window is displayed, click on the link to access the auth.html window. Login as qatest1 and test1. Attempt to login as qatest2 and test2.
